evidence:
[1] Integrated ASHA Training Module – Part B — page 189
Danger Signs During Early Pregnancy
Decreased/absent foetal movements is an emergency and she must report immediately to the nearest health facility. Some important high risk pregnancies : Anaemia is an extremely common condition among women , especially pregnant women. It occurs when haemoglobin levels in the blood are low, reducing oxygen supply to the body. A haemoglobin level below 11 g/dl during first and third trimester and below 10.5 g/dl during second trimester of pregnancy indicates anaemia. Anaemia increases the risk of infections, pre-eclampsia, bleeding , low birth weight, prematurity, fetal distress, and even maternal and neonatal death. Severe anaemia can lead to heart failure. A woman with anaemia looks pale, feels tired, complains of breathlessness on exertion . In severe anemia , she may feel breathless even on doing routine work and might have swelling on the face and body. The most common causes are poor dietary intake of iron, folate and vitamin B12, repeated infections, worm infestation, blood loss, and hereditary blood disorders. The level of hemoglobin can be tested by a simple blood test, which is undertaken by the ANM in AAM-HSC or the lab technician at the PHC -AAM .

[2] Induction Training Module for ASHA — page 68
8.1 Care During Pregnancy/Ante Natal Care
l Anaemia is due to a reduced level of haemoglobin in the blood. Haemoglobin is a substance in the blood that carries oxygen which is important for all body functions. The amount of haemoglobin can be tested by a simple blood test, which the ANM in the health sub-centre or a lab technician in a health facility will do. Anaemia in the Young Child
Anaemia is important to diagnose because it commonly comes along with malnutrition. It may be a cause of poor appetite. Blood testing is essential, but even in its absence based on observation of pallor alone, treatment can be started. Unusual paleness (Pallor) of the skin of the soles or palms is a sign of anaemia. • To see if the child has anaemia, look at the skin of the child’s palm. Hold the child’s palm open by grasping it gently from side to side. • Do not stretch the fingers backward. This may cause pallor. • Compare the child’s palm with your own palm and the palm of other children. If the skin is paler than of others, the child has pallor. Treatment for anaemia is to give one tablet of paediatric iron daily. And also give one tablet of Albendazole for deworming once in six months. For a child less than two years, give half a tablet of Albendazole (Refer Annexure 6). Iron rich foods as discussed for the mother (Book 6) are also needed for the young child.
